scope: Main paper and references on pages 1-28; appendix bodies excluded.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Let $\|\cdot\|$ and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ denote the Euclidean norm and inner product, respectively. Let $B_d(x,r):=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:\|y-x\|\le r\}$ denote the closed ball with center $x$ and radius $r$. We use $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm F}$ for the operator and Frobenius norms of matrices, respectively. For a topological space $S$, $\mathcal P(S)$ denotes the class of Borel probability measures on it.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: Theorem 1 uses the Frobenius norm, not the operator norm. Matrix A has shape d_x by d_y. Euclidean spaces, product measures and integrals are ambient. The theorem-local box D_M is explicitly defined inside its statement.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be two Polish spaces and consider a lower semicontinuous cost function $c:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\to\mathbb R$, where note that we allow $c$ to take negative value.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: This is the setup for the EOT definition used in Theorem 1. The cost c_A is polynomial and can be negative; no nonnegative-cost convention is imported. Extra hypotheses used to establish a separate OT duality statement are not prerequisites of the EOT primal definition.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: For $p\in[1,\infty)$ and $\rho\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d)$, let $L^p(\rho)$ be the space of measurable functions $f$ of $\mathbb R^d$ such that $\|f\|_{L^p(\rho)}:=(\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f|^p\,d\rho)^{1/p}<\infty$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: The GW formulas use the same integral norm construction on the appropriate product space. The p in a function-space norm is distinct from an index labeling components of the EGW decomposition.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.source_heading: Section 1.4 — comparison constants and dimension operations
unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We use $\lesssim_x$ to denote inequalities up to constants that only depend on $x$; the subscript is dropped when the constant is universal. For $a,b\in\mathbb R$, let $a\vee b=\max\{a,b\}$ and $a\wedge b=\min\{a,b\}$.

evidence.location: Section 1.4 — comparison constants and dimension operations

unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: Upper-bound constants in Theorems 2 and 3 are dimension-indexed. Theorem 3 lower-bound constants additionally list R. The one-sample exponent uses d_x, while its two-sample exponent uses the smaller dimension. Ceilings and indicator functions are ordinary mathematical binders.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: With the setup above, we have $\mathsf S_0(\mu,\nu)=\mathsf D(\mu,\nu)^2$
unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: The entropic functional has the units of squared GW distortion, not of the unsquared distance. This passage supplies the zero-regularization convention; no KL penalty evaluated as an undefined zero-times-infinity expression is silently substituted.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.source_heading: Before Theorem 1 — meaning of the two components
unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Evidently, the first term depends only on the marginals $\mu,
u$, while the second captures the dependence on the coupling $\pi$. The following theorem establishes duality for $\mathsf S_\varepsilon^2(\mu,
u)$, which, in turn, yields a dual form for $\mathsf S_\varepsilon(\mu,
u)$ via the above decomposition.

evidence.location: Before Theorem 1 — meaning of the two components

unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: The superscript 2 labels the coupling-dependent component from (8), rather than a square. Theorem 1 is about that component. The whole EGW functional is obtained by adding the first component.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: In particular, $\rho$ is sub-Gaussian if it is 2-sub-Weibull. Notice that $X\sim\rho$ being 4-sub-Weibull is equivalent to $\|X\|^2$ being sub-Gaussian, in which case $\int e^{t\|x\|^2}\,d\rho(x)\le2e^{t^2\sigma^2/2}$. The latter bound is repeatedly used in our derivations.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: Theorem 2 uses the source exponential-norm definition with beta=4. Do not replace it by a generic sub-Gaussian assumption on X or reinterpret sigma squared as the variance of X. This auxiliary explanatory source assertion is preserved without being promoted to another Theorem.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: and if $\mu,\nu$ are separated in the $(2,2)$-GW distance, i.e., $\mathsf D(\mu,\nu)>0$, then the same rates hold for estimating $\mathsf D$ itself, without the square.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.note: This extra clause is already included in the full original theorem. It does not assert the same unsquared-distance rates uniformly near zero separation. Separation does not mean disjoint supports in a common Euclidean space.

source_issues: The source is the verified 47-page arXiv:2212.12848v3 PDF with the printed stamp 28 September 2023. The original versioned URL and existing stable theorem/interface IDs are retained. The prior migration audit did not perform fresh PDF review; those four artifacts are preserved under prior-review.
The main paper includes references through page 28, ending with [ZMGS22]. Appendix A starts on page 29. Bookmarks and the appendix heading locate the boundary without reading appendix bodies.

Three and only three bold main-text Theorem environments occur: Theorems 1 and 2 on page 9 and Theorem 3 on page 11. Main-text Propositions, Lemmas, Corollary 1 and regular-font citations to external Theorems are not inventoried as Theorems.

All original theorem bodies match the PDF and are retained. Theorem 3 includes both upper bounds, the strictly positive GW separation clause and both sharpness lower bounds. None of these statements continues onto the next page.

Theorem 1 uses the second component S_epsilon^2 of the EGW decomposition. Its superscript 2 is a component label, while D(mu,nu)^2 in Theorem 3 is an actual square. The component can have a negative value and should not be treated as a nonnegative squared distance.

Section 3.2 centers both marginals before deriving (8). The new D12 source condition records this convention and the D6 dependency. Theorem 1 itself opens with fourth-moment membership without restating centering; the original statement is not rewritten or strengthened.

The full EGW functional is invariant to translations, but its displayed moment formulas and decomposition must be interpreted with the stated centering convention. In particular, recentering does not leave raw second and fourth moments unchanged. The empirical error theorems do not acquire a zero-sample-mean assumption from this argument.

D6 now also resolves its left side S_epsilon to the original entropic functional D5. D7 resolves its named OT_A,epsilon problem to the EOT definition D3. These links complete source dependencies omitted from the earlier graph without importing proof-only regularity classes.

Theorem 1 explicitly assumes fourth absolute moments but defines M_mu,nu with second absolute moments. Its matrix optimization is over all real d_x-by-d_y matrices, and it separately asserts attainment in the closed coordinatewise box [-M_mu,nu/2,M_mu,nu/2]^(d_x times d_y). This is not a Frobenius-norm ball.

The EOT cost is -4 times the product of squared norms minus 32 x-transpose A y. Negative costs are allowed by the preceding Section 2.1 setup. The regularization is strictly positive and the reference measure is the product of the two marginals.

Couplings have specified first and second marginals. GW distortion uses the product of the same coupling with itself, not two independently optimized couplings. The quadratic Euclidean distance D takes the square root after integration and minimization; S_epsilon has no square root.

The original definitions retain the Euclidean fourth-moment domain, absolute moments and the product-measure KL penalty. KL is plus infinity when absolute continuity fails. No centered/debiased Sinkhorn divergence or symmetrized entropy is substituted.

The sub-Weibull definition uses the exponential of norm-to-beta divided by 2 sigma squared and allows sigma>=0. The sigma=0 endpoint has no explicit division-by-zero convention in this passage. Theorem 2 avoids that endpoint by requiring sigma squared>0 and beta=4 for both populations.

Theorem 2 exponents are 9 ceil(d_x/2)+11 and 9 ceil((d_x vee d_y)/2)+11. A magnified PDF review confirmed the placement of the ceiling and the addition of eleven. The numerator outside the entropy term is 1+sigma^4, and the regularization multiplier is epsilon.

Theorem 2 has one- and two-sample expected absolute-error bounds for the full S_epsilon functional. The populations need not be compactly supported. The two-sample bound uses the larger dimension inside a constant exponent, while both sample-size rates are n^(-1/2).

The empirical measures use equal sample size n and the source wording independently and identically distributed samples from mu and nu, respectively. No paired-sample dependence model or unequal sample-size extension is inferred.

Theorem 3 concerns compact subsets of potentially different Euclidean spaces and uses R as the maximum of their diameters. Its one-sample exponent is 2/(d_x vee 4); its two-sample exponent is 2/((d_x wedge d_y) vee 4). Logarithmic factors occur exactly at the corresponding dimension-four threshold.

Theorem 3 lower bounds omit the upper-bound logarithmic factor and take a supremum over the populations for the empirical estimator. They are not minimax lower bounds over all estimators. The printed lower-bound scope only names compact supports; no full-dimensionality or nondegeneracy assumption is stated.

The asserted lower bounds require care for degenerate or finite compact supports, where an ambient-dimension rate need not be sharp. This source-scope issue is retained separately; no unstated geometric hypothesis is inserted into the original theorem or graph.

The separated-population clause requires D(mu,nu)>0. It concerns estimation of D without the square, not an additional lower-bound claim valid uniformly at zero separation. Any resulting dependence on inverse separation should not be suppressed when interpreting the rate.
The sum defining S_epsilon^2 on page 8 prints d_1 and d_2, while the surrounding spaces use d_x and d_y. This source index mismatch is preserved, rather than silently changing a quoted formula.

Euclidean and Frobenius norms, Borel probabilities, product measures, Lp integral norms, ordinary expectation, dimension min/max, indicator functions, ceiling and diameter are resolved by source context or ambient conventions. The theorem-local matrix box, radius R, parameters and rate quantities are not invented APIs.

OT/EOT dual potentials, Schrodinger equations, regularity classes, covering estimates, Wasserstein-Procrustes reductions and auxiliary lemmas are used in the proofs. They do not become statement dependencies merely because the proof uses them, and no appendix detail is imported.

The new census retains all ten previous interface IDs and adds only the source centering condition. Source wording is preserved with harmless TeX spacing normalization. All source kinds, keywords, highlights, local paths and explanations are rebuilt and source-checked rather than accepted solely from the prior migration audit.

statement_resolution.1: D6 resolves the second component of (8), together with D12 centering and D5 the whole EGW functional. D3 and D7 resolve the EOT objective and its explicit cost. D10 resolves P4, M2 and the locally bound M_mu,nu. A is a theorem-bound real matrix and D_M its explicitly defined coordinate box; A1 supplies the Frobenius norm. No EOT-potential theorem is a statement dependency.
statement_resolution.2: D5 resolves the full entropic functional and its domain via D4,D10. D8 supplies empirical measures and the sampling convention. D9 is the explicit beta=4 source tail condition with a common positive parameter. Epsilon, sigma and n are theorem/section binders. A4 explains constants, ceiling and dimension maximum. Neither D6 nor D12 is a hypothesis of this empirical statement.
statement_resolution.3: D4 resolves the quadratic GW distance, D8 the empirical measures. The compact supports and their maximum diameter R are bound in the theorem. A4 resolves min/max and hidden-constant notation; A8 records the already preserved positive-separation clause. The displayed lower-bound supremum ranges over measures, not over estimators. Its source support-geometry scope remains explicit.

unresolved_source_references.reason: Centering is explicit in the preceding convention and preserved separately, without rewriting the theorem.
The component sum uses indices different from the surrounding d_x,d_y notation.
The source gives no division-by-zero convention; Theorem 2 assumes a positive parameter.
Only compactness is explicit; the printed dimension-dependent sharpness assertion needs care for finite or degenerate supports.
No appendix body or external proof is needed to preserve the original statement inventory and its main-text dependencies.
